title: Tailored POC Journey Map and Facilitation Cheat Sheet
content:
Purpose:
- Lightweight facilitator-facing runbook to run a 2-day customer POC sprint (remote or onsite) focused on validating inference economics + reliability for an initial integration.

Objectives:
- Validate latency and cost envelope on a representative workload (sample queries)
- Confirm routing/fallback policy for capacity constraints
- Produce a go/no-go deployment recommendation and next-step roadmap with tangible success criteria

High-level hypothesis (for customer kickoff):
- "If we serve the top-10 query patterns with Redwood Dedicated with prefix KV cache enabled, then 95th-pct latency will be <120ms and per-token cost will be <= target X given expected QPS"

Pre-work (owner: SE lead, due 3 business days before kickoff):
- Customer: provide 48-72 hour sample of production traffic OR 2000 representative prompts and labels (anonymize)
- Infra: verify account has sandbox dedicated pool or access to hosted test model variants
- SE: prepare 6 slide deck (see slide map), test runner notebook, and a short health-check script (latency & token counters)

Attendees:
- Solutions Engineer (facilitator) — run experiments, capture metrics
- Customer Engineering Lead — provides context and validates queries
- Product/Infra SME (optional) — answers deployment questions
- Customer PM / Stakeholder — decision maker for go/no-go

Day 0: Pre-kickoff checklist (30–60m sync)
- Confirm dataset uploaded and reachable
- Confirm test credentials and endpoint access
- Smoke run: 10 synthetic queries to ensure pipeline is live

Day 1 (Discovery + Quick Experiments) — 4.5 hours- 09:00 Introductions & success criteria (15m): align metrics (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, quality thresholds)
- 09:15 Architecture walkthrough (20m): customer infra, where the inference call fits, network paths, auth
- 09:40 Test plan & experiment schedule (10m): define buckets (small/medium/long seqs), routing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated), and fallback triggers
- 09:50 Baseline run (40m): run sample through hosted model (no caching, default batching). Capture latency, token counts, failure modes.
- 10:35 Quick-win optimizations (40m): enable prefix cache on subset (top-10 prompts), enable light batching, compare p95 improvement
- 11:20 Quality spot-check (25m): manual review of outputs for 50 representative prompts (customer & SE)
- 11:50 Lunch
- 12:30 Deeper experiments (90m): dedicated pool test (quantization variant if available), routing policy simulation, throttling/fallback injection
- 14:00 Data capture & breakouts (30m): split SEs to debug anomalies, produce metric summary
- 14:30 Synthesis & next-action list (30m): what to stress next on Day 2, hardware/parameter changes required

Day 2 (Stress, Validation, Recommendation) — 4 hours
- 09:00 Ramp & chaos tests (60m): increase QPS to target peak, simulate region outage or capacity evictions, validate fallback works and SLAs hold
- 10:00 Cost analysis (30m): calculate per-100k-token and per-hour cost for each config tested, include caching and batching multipliers
- 10:30 Regression check & quality hold (30m): ensure recommended config does not drop quality beyond agreed threshold
- 11:00 Roadmap & ops handoff (30m): list infra changes, monitoring queries, alert thresholds, required infra commit levels for Dedicated
- 11:30 Final recommendation & decision toggle (30m): go/no-go criteria: if p95 < target and cost within budget, recommend deployment; else list mitigations and follow-up experiments

Slide map (6–8 slides) — speaker notes included:
- Slide 1: Title + Sprint goals (speaker: SE) — 1-liner goal, list of attendees, timebox
- Slide 2: Hypothesis + Acceptance criteria (speaker: Customer lead + SE) — be explicit: latency p95 target, cost target, quality thresholds
- Slide 3: Test matrix & experiment plan (speaker: SE) — show buckets: seq length, throughput targets, routing variants
- Slide 4: Baseline metrics (speaker: SE) — p50/p95 latency, error rates, per-token counts, sample outputs (good/bad)
- Slide 5: Optimization delta (speaker: SE) — caching/batching/quantization effect on metrics, incremental cost impact
- Slide 6: Resilience & fallbacks (speaker: Infra SME) — what happens on region failure, model variant fallback, circuit-breaker rules
- Slide 7: Ops/runbook & monitoring (speaker: SE) — required dashboards, alert thresholds, what to escalate and how
- Slide 8: Recommendation & next steps (speaker: Customer PM + SE) — checklist for deployment, owners, dates

Facilitation cheat-sheet (tips & scripts):
- Run timers visibly. Keep experiments time-boxed (30–90m windows).
- When output quality disagreement arises, use a short 5-sample adjudication: customer scores outputs 1–5; median <=3 triggers rollback metric
- Use "session tags" in experiments to simplify metric grouping (e.g., custX_day1_cache_on)
- If p95 unstable, prioritize investigating sequence length distribution and KV cache key affinity
- For remote customers: share a single Notion/Google Sheet with live metric table and links to logs; ask customer to mark blockers with emoji

Failure modes & mitigation playbook (quick lookups):
- High p95 but low p50: likely batching misconfiguration or heterogeneous request sizes -> reduce max-batch-latency or split by seq length
- Elevated error rate under load: memory pressure or model oom -> try quantized variant or increase pool size; collect kernel logs
- Quality regressions after quantization: reduce quant level or hybrid route small-number tail queries to FP16 variant

Artifacts to produce during/after sprint (owner tag):
- Experiment CSV export with session tags (owner: SE)
- Slide deck updated with final metrics (owner: SE)
- Short deployment runbook (owner: Infra SME)
- Follow-up Jira epic with backlog items and owners (owner: Customer PM)
content_summary: Two-day PO C sprint plan: objectives, pre-work, detailed hourly agenda, slide map with speaker notes, facilitation tips, failure-mode playbook, and post-sprint artifacts
notes: Informal draft — intended to be adapted per-customer. Keep copies short and iterative. Link any long-running performance dumps to Confluence pages rather than embedding raw logs.
